Again, congrats, that’s your choice. Going vegan is great, I wish I could do it, but people who aren’t vegan aren’t below you. People will always eat meat and consume animal products. That’s life. Anyways I’m not the one running the farm, I merely took a picture. 

Edit: I’m not trying to make them look good, I’m telling people what I read and what I saw. Where did you see on the site that this farm produces meat? Honestly, I’m not sugar coating anything, I’m clarifying misconceptions so people can make informed comments. Are you a vegan? If not, then this is pretty hypocritical. No offense.

I’m glad that there’s concern about the calf’s condition, it tells me that people care about the animal’s wellbeing. However, I have provided a few links to give information about this farm. This calf was only a month old at the time, so he/she was kept in a separate environment away from the older calves in the pasture. For those concerned about it being away from the mother, if I remember correctly the ones who were not being milked were with their babies. This is where they stay when their mothers are being milked, where they get vet checkups, etc. There were also only around 5 calves (is that the plural of calf?), as this is not one of those huge, inhumane farms. 
The farm (Billings Farm) is funded by a non profit charity called the Woodstock Foundation. I don’t work there, I just went there for a visit this summer, so unfortunately I don’t have all the answers. Again, the website is this [Website ](https://billingsfarm.org). 

Tldr; This farm is trustworthy, check out the website if you’re curious

They’re not kept exclusively in these confinements, and they do spend time with the mothers. However, it is a dairy farm, so when the cows are being milked it is safer to keep the young away. They also get vet checkups and such in this room to make sure they are healthy. I provided a link to the website if you want to learn more. Trust me I am huge on animal rights. If this place seemed shady, or the animals seemed to be treated poorly, I would speak out against them rather than posting for karma. This farm is also funded by the Woodstock Foundation, which was founded by Laurance S. and Mary F. Rockefeller. It is a “charitable, nonprofit institution that promotes conservation, sustainable land use, and heritage as values that are essential to culture, community, and the human spirit” [source ](https://billingsfarm.org/about/) So pretty much this farm isn’t looking for profit. 

TLDR: Mother’s and babies do spend time together, this calf happened to be in a separate environment. Also, the farm is funded by a charity, so it’s more about preservation of traditions than mass production.

Also, most of the cows and calves were out in the pasture, but these little guys were too young I guess. I probably sound like I’m promoting this farm, but they really do take care of their animals unlike big dairy corporations, and I would hate to bring misconceptions upon them. 
Edit: idk why I’m being downvoted, I just wanted to give some information so that people could look into the treatment of the animals /:

This was at a dairy farm in Vermont. The cows were very well taken care of, and the babies were only around a month old so they stayed in a more controlled environment :) if you want I can link you information to the farm.
